nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages for misclassification.
A model generated during the first pass analysis based on which folder each message resides and other message attributes; it resides exclusively in non-persistent memory and is purged after use.

A message filter configured to sort messages into different message folders and store first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A message filter that previously sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A message filter configured to sort messages into different message folders and to store first classification data in a persistent store.
A filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis, perform a second pass to identify misclassified messages, and purge the model from non-persistent memory.

A device distinct from a client device on which the first message filter is configured to execute.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform multi-pass message filtering actions.<SEP>A device configured to receive messages, assign them to message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over the network to the message folders.
A component of the network device that sends and receives data over a network.
A component of the network device operative to perform actions including first pass analysis, second pass analysis, displaying misclassification identification, and purging the classification model.

A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and inspected by the multi-pass filter.<SEP>Different folders into which messages are sorted, and to which identified incorrectly sorted messages may be moved by a user.
A generated identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, displayed so a user can move misclassified messages to a different folder.
A memory-resident-only location where the generated classification model resides exclusively, not stored on disk or another persistent data store.

A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A storage location where the first classification data is stored by the first message filter.

A device on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and where the first and second passes may occur entirely.<SEP>A device that executes the passes of the multi-pass message filter, generates and stores second classification data, scores messages, identifies incorrectly sorted messages, and displays associated information.

A storage medium readable by a processor that stores instructions for executing the multi-pass message filter.<SEP>A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.
An email or similar item sorted into folders, analyzed for sender information, headers, subject, originating network address, contents, and attachments.
Information within messages read during the first pass, including the sender's address and whether it is in an address book associated with a recipient.
Header information within messages, including a subject, read during the first pass analysis.
The contents of messages read during the first pass analysis.<SEP>The content of a message that may be analyzed as a basis for generating second classification data.
Attachments within messages read during the first pass analysis.

An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used to analyze whether a message sender's address is present.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis for generating second classification data.

A person whose mail folders are scanned and who is presented a list of messages that might be misclassified so they can move messages to different folders.<SEP>A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder and able to select execution of the multi-pass message filter through an interface.
A recipient associated with the message folders and with an address book used in classification analysis.

A message filtering method that operates in multiple passes, employing a Naive Bayes classifier and trained by generating second classification data from sorted messages.<SEP>A message filter executed in multiple passes on a client device; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message.
A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter.
Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.

Classification data generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train it, and which can be deleted so it is no longer accessible.<SEP>Classification data generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and used to score messages in the second pass.
A model generated based on an analysis of at least which message folder a message currently resides.
One of a plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted, and whose current residence of a message is analyzed for generating the second classification model.

A method for managing message delivery comprising receiving messages, sorting them into folders using a first message filter, and executing a first pass of a multi-pass message filter on a client device.<SEP>A method for managing message delivery that involves receiving messages, sorting them into folders using a first message filter, and executing a multi-pass message filter on a client device to identify messages sorted into incorrect folders.
A memory store on the client device where the second classification data resides exclusively.
A score assigned to each message by the second pass of the multi-pass message filter, used to determine whether a message is sorted into an incorrect message folder.
A message folder into which a message has been incorrectly sorted, as indicated by the message's score.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select execution of the multi-pass message filter.
An address of a message sender that may be analyzed, including whether it is in an address book associated with a recipient, as a basis for generating second classification data.
A header of a message that may be analyzed as a basis for generating second classification data.
A state of a message that may be analyzed as a basis for generating second classification data.
A system for enabling communications over a network, comprising a network device and a client device.
A network over which messages are communicated between the network device and the client device.
